This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/data/related-list-body-table.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-driven.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/data/related-list-body-table.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 141a826f4c124187c2a3af253dc5a95f9d3818d7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8d69c6f66ff15fa2f612c6c424462db8f0a01c0b` — the merge of head `97afed5aab44ab898b1c29ea8429ad056fcdb981` into base `141a826f4c124187c2a3af253dc5a95f9d3818d7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8d69c6f66ff15fa2f612c6c424462db8f0a01c0b && git checkout 8d69c6f66ff15fa2f612c6c424462db8f0a01c0b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 141a826f4c124187c2a3af253dc5a95f9d3818d7 97afed5aab44ab898b1c29ea8429ad056fcdb981 && git checkout -B drift-repro 141a826f4c124187c2a3af253dc5a95f9d3818d7 && git merge --no-ff 97afed5aab44ab898b1c29ea8429ad056fcdb981

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 141a826f4c124187c2a3af253dc5a95f9d3818d7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 141a826f4c124187c2a3af253dc5a95f9d3818d7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

- 要你做什么：现在不需要。合并前还要过席位的 Fable 复审和 os-zhuang 的批准。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT (L1-c) · repo:objectstack#1 · head `84dc199e27` · 2026-11-21T07:07Z

Read at `84dc199e27`: 18 files against `main`. It touches `docs/adr/**` and `packages/spec/src/**`, so it is Tier H. This is an L1 only: the seat runs the Fable L2 on this head, and os-zhuang approves.

I first read `11ee7b5f1b`, then the delta to `84dc199e27`. It holds `25b2e82f`, the merge of `main` (`9f3f7852`, read with `--remerge-diff`), the reference regeneration (`6d0988c0`), and `84dc199e`, a test-only import that loads `@object-ui/react-runtime` at collection time.

### Found in the read, fixed at `25b2e82f`

- **The portal put the line grid inside the header `<form>`.** At `11ee7b5f1b` the header's `requestSubmit()` (no `noValidate`) would have run native constraint validation over the line cells. A `badInput` number or date cell could then have stopped Save at a browser bubble, before react-hook-form's `onSubmit` ran.
- **The fix.** `FormSlotPlacement` now portals the collection inside a wrapper `<form noValidate onSubmit={preventDefault}>` whose first child is a disabled, hidden default button. So:
  - every line control's form owner is the wrapper, not the header, and the header validates only its own fields;
  - a line button without a `type` submits only the wrapper, which does nothing;
  - Enter in a cell meets the disabled default button, so implicit submission does nothing.
- **The expanded row editor.** It keeps its own `<form>` as the owner of its inputs. Its React submit bubbles to the wrapper's `preventDefault`, which is harmless next to react-hook-form's own.
- **Reveal on refusal.** `form.tsx`'s `fieldWrapper` now skips a `[data-field]` that sits in one of this form's own slot rows. So a header refusal scrolls to the header's field, never to a same-named line-editor field, and an editor inside a slot still finds its own fields.
- **Pins.**
  - `MasterDetailForm.groupPlacement-35889` asserts `control.form !== header` for every input, select, textarea and button in the slot, and that clicking every slot button fires no header `submit`.
  - `form-invalid-scroll` pins the reveal: the form's own field is scrolled to, and the slotted twin is neither scrolled to nor focused.

### Merge and regeneration

The only file the merge resolved by hand is `content/docs/references/data/object.mdx`, which took the branch's side of the `highlightFields` row. `6d0988c0` then regenerated it, and the row now matches `main` (#35977's text). Nothing else in the merge differs from the automatic result.

### Nits

- **Tabbed form.** A line-row refusal raised on Save can sit in a tab that is not active. If the existing refusal path does not already switch tabs or name the tab, a follow-up card is enough.
- **The rule is in two places.** `placeFormSlots` and `bodyTablePlacement` both decide where a group-placed table sits. The body already names this as a follow-up candidate. Fine as a follow-up.

### Checked and fine

- **Shape.** Draft, base `main`. `Fixes #35889` is right: this is S2, it delivers acceptance line 2 (the entry form places the table at its group), and S1 (#35921) was `Part of`.
- **Placement.**
  - `placeFormSlots(sections, sectionGroupKey, fieldGroups, requests)` puts a slot after the sections of the groups declared before its group and before those declared after it. That is the record page's `bodyTablePlacement` rule.
  - A section that names no declared group (the ungrouped bucket, an authored section) counts as after every group.
  - Sections keep their order, and slots at one position keep the request order.
  - A layout none of whose sections names a declared group places nothing, so the table stays below the fields.
  - `claim` runs once per drawn layout and never while loading, so a remounting header does not make the table jump.
  - `formSlots.test.ts` (6 cases) covers these. `MasterDetailForm.groupPlacement-35889.test.tsx` (6 cases) runs it through the real `MasterDetailForm` → `ObjectForm` → `form.tsx` chain, flat and tabbed.
- **The `form-slot` row.** `form.tsx` renders an empty `div[data-form-slot]` and keeps it out of the drawn and changeable sets, so it adds no value, no dirty state and no section-nav item. `splitAtUntitledRuns` gives it a block of its own after the heading that claims its fields.
- **The header scrape.** `scrapeHeaderRecord` skips `[data-form-slot]`, so line inputs never leak into the header record. `handleSave`'s `querySelector('form')` still returns the header form, which comes first in document order.
- **Keyboard.** Every `GridField` button is `type="button"`, Enter in a cell calls `preventDefault`, and the header is built with `showSubmit: false`. Since `25b2e82f` the wrapper form backs all three.
- **Contract text.** The `ObjectFieldGroupSchema.relatedList` and `FieldSchema.relatedList` describe and JSDoc, the `related-list-body-table.ts` header and its describe pin, the regenerated `object.mdx`, and the acceptance line of semantic migration `semantic/18.master-detail-related-list-tab-by-default` now say the form places the table at its group. The migration text cites no `#ids`. The ADR-0035 note is add-only: S1's sentences stay as written, and the note names the one it supersedes.
- **Changesets.**
  - `.changeset/35889-form-places-detail-at-group.md` is new and declares `@object-ui/plugin-form`, `@object-ui/components` and `@objectstack/spec`, all `patch`. That matches the shipped JSDoc and describe text. I read it sentence by sentence against the diff.
  - **Deliberate correction, checked.** `Check Changeset` is red because one line of `.changeset/35889-master-detail-tab-by-default.md` (S1, #35921, merged and still pending on `main`) is rewritten. The old line said the entry form still put the table below the fields, and this PR makes that false. The new line matches the diff, including the fallback for a form whose sections name no group. The body declares it under "DELIBERATE CORRECTION". The seat's ACCEPT will carry the confirmation, so restoring the old line is not owed.
- **Evidence.** Screenshots exist at 1280 and 375. `between-light-375` shows the table between the groups around it.
- **Overlap watch.** `buildDefaultPageSchema.ts` and `RecordDetailView` are untouched. `related-list-body-table.ts` changes in text only.

### Gates

At `84dc199e27`: 61 success, 11 expected skips, 0 pending. The only red is `Check Changeset`, twice (two runs). Both logs fail on exactly one file, `.changeset/35889-master-detail-tab-by-default.md`, which is the deliberate correction confirmed above, so that red is by design. `mergeable_state` is `unstable` only because of it. l1-face flags that check and nothing else.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of `@objectstack/spec`: unchanged. Right.** The five spec hunks are text only: the jsdoc on `FieldSchema.relatedList`, the jsdoc and the `.describe()` string on `ObjectFieldGroupSchema.relatedList`, the header comment of `related-list-body-table.ts`, and the `acceptanceCriteria` string of migration entry `semantic/18`. Right.** `id`, `surface`, `replacement` and `reason` are untouched; the changeset gate's level axis reports "moves no metadata-protocol baseline" on this head, which agrees with `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- **Public surface of `@object-ui/plugin-form` and `@object-ui/components`: no new export. Right.** `formSlots.ts` is imported only by `MasterDetailForm.tsx`, `ObjectForm.tsx` and `TabbedForm.tsx`; the hand-off key `formSlots` is typed in that module (`FormSlotHandoff`) and is not added to `ObjectFormSchema` in `@object-ui/types`. The form renderer learns one row type, `form-slot`, that only a host can produce (its `slotRef` is a function, never authorable metadata).
- **Behaviour derived for consumers: a group-placed collection moves from below the header form to inside it. Right, and bounded.** It moves only when the header's drawn layout has at least one section naming a declared field group AND a field group names the collection; every other form keeps the old place (`placeFormSlots` returns `plain`, the header claims `[]`, `FormSlotStore.placement` answers `'inline'`). - `Metadata-protocol: none` on both: right, see ①.
- **The DELIBERATE CORRECTION of `.changeset/35889-master-detail-tab-by-default.md` is confirmed.** One line changes; the rest of the note is byte-identical. The sentence it replaces ("a placed table still sits below the record's fields ... Moving it to its group's place in the form is a follow-up") is false on this head, so restoring it would publish a false release note. The corrected sentence, clause by clause against the diff:

**Spec hits against the implementing code, sentence by sentence.**

Form ownership is answered by the wrapper form in `FormSlotPlacement` (`noValidate`, a disabled hidden default button, `preventDefault`), pinned in the DOM test; React events from the portal follow the React tree (`MasterDetailLines`), not the header, so the header's handlers never see line events; the three DOM reads that cross the boundary are each fenced (`scrapeHeaderRecord` skips `[data-form-slot]`, `fieldWrapper` skips fields inside this form's slots while a nested editor still finds its own, and `formHostRef.querySelector('form')` returns the header form because an ancestor precedes its descendants in document order).
